marc (Eng Manager): Quick one: we promoted an IC to L5 while they were on parental leave. Their manager submitted late because of timing. Can we make the comp effective during leave, or do we have to backdate?
lina (People Ops): Good question. We can set the effective date to the intended promotion date (even if the person is on leave) but you must include manager + director sign-off and the calibration packet. Payroll will do a retro adjustment to pay any difference once comp change is approved.
sasha (Compensation): To add: for promotions whose effective date falls during statutory leave, we confirm with Benefits that benefit-eligible components (like 401k matching) are applied correctly. Equity grants follow our normal grant schedule and may require the next grant cycle if cutoff missed.
marc (Eng Manager): ok. what about cases where the manager forgot to include rubric evidence? they want the level now but we only have sparse notes.
tom (Recruiter): reminder: do NOT pull offer paperwork or send amended letters until People Ops confirms the change. It causes confusion.
sasha (Compensation): If evidence is missing we triage as an "incomplete packet". People Ops will request missing rubric examples; committee won't rule until packet is complete. If manager can provide 3 concrete examples mapped to the leveling rubric within 5 business days we can keep the original effective date in many cases.
jordi (Finance): note on retro pay: payroll cutoff is the 10th. Retro for prior months posts on the next payroll after Finance receives the approved adj. Also, larger headcount/band impacts may need budget owner sign-off; flag early if this is >$20k annual run rate.
marc (Eng Manager): good to know. Another edge: person got promoted AND changed role (IC -> people manager) mid-cycle. Do we treat as promotion + role change? separate approvals?
lina (People Ops): Role changes that include a managerial responsibility require manager + director + People Ops approval and a skip-level acknowledgement. Compensation reviews both base and any new managerial allowances. If it's a hybrid (title change with level bump) annotate that in the packet so Compensation can evaluate band placement.
sasha (Compensation): For hybrid moves we look at scope delta. If scope expands significantly, committee may propose a higher band or phased increase. We also consider internal parity with direct reports; attach peer comps if available.
marc (Eng Manager): is there an easy checklist I can forward to managers to avoid incomplete submissions?
lina (People Ops): yes — checklist (copy/paste for DMs): 1) Complete /forms/promo-request and pick "Outside cycle" if not in planned cycle. 2) Attach calibration notes and 3 example evidence mapped to rubric. 3) Director sign-off (email or sign field). 4) Org chart + reporting lines. 5) Indicate effective date and whether employee is on leave. 6) Recruiter confirms offer letter hold / no changes until approval. 7) Budget owner pinged if >$20k ARR impact.
sasha (Compensation): I'll also send managers a one-page matrix of examples per level to speed mapping.
payroll-bot: Heads up: any approved adjustments submitted to Finance before 10th -> included in same month payroll. After 10th -> processed next month.
marc (Eng Manager): thanks everyone. One last: if manager wants to appeal a committee decision, what's the path?
lina (People Ops): Appeals: submit a follow-up packet via the same form within 14 days of decision and include new evidence + director rationale. Appeals after 14 days require exec sponsor. Appeals rarely overturn without material new evidence.
sasha (Compensation): FYI equity appeals are escalated to Total Rewards and may take longer due to grant schedules.
jordi (Finance): happy to do a quick budget sanity check before you submit — ping me with the estimated run-rate.
lina (People Ops): I'll post the checklist and the promo playbook link in #people-ops when live. Thanks all.
